03.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3.
The petitioner has filed this writ petition with the following prayer:

"It is, therefore, humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to Issue Rule NISI calling upon the Opp.Parties to show cause as to why; (I) Why the Opp.Parties shall not be directed to implement the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and further why Resettlement and Rehabilitation Scheme prepared for the project by providing Ac. 0.10 Dce Homestead land and Ac.
2.00 Acres extent of agriculture land to the petitioner as per the provision of the scheme or in alternative to compensate the petitioner as per the present market value of the land within a stipulated time and extend the other benefits not yet provided and it the Opp. Parties failed to show cause or show insufficient or false cause make the Rule NISI absolute and allow this writ petition with cost."
4.

As agreed by learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court,
without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, disposes of the Writ Petition directing Opposite Party No.6 to consider and dispose of the representation filed by the petitioner vide Annexure-7 Series and pass appropriate order as early as possible within a period of three months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
